source_title: Evaluating alternative resource allocation in an emergency department using discrete event simulation
locator: Process description and Table 1, ESI assignment and required staff/test matrix
source_setting: One US metropolitan ED; model calibrated to a 24-hour ED averaging 115 patients/day
quantity: Modeled acuity-dependent role and test requirements

value.ESI1: 1 physician, 2 nurses, 1 EMT; blood, X-ray, CT (70% modeled)
value.ESI2: 1 physician, 2 nurses, 1 EMT; blood, X-ray, CT (70% modeled)
value.ESI3: 1 physician, 1 nurse; blood, X-ray, CT (30% modeled)
value.ESI5: 1 physician assistant, 1 nurse; no listed test

unit: staff/test slots per simulated patient; conditional CT share (%)
source_evidence_basis: The authors describe an ED-specific DES built from patient severity, staff interviews, and observed workflow. Its local ESI matrix assigns different staff roles and diagnostics by acuity; ESI 1–2 have physician, nurse, EMT and blood/X-ray/CT requirements, whereas ESI 4–5 route to a PA with a nurse and less testing.
limitations: This is one site’s model specification, not measured universal protocol or observed simultaneous concurrency. Authors assume equipment is fully operational and staff available without breaks; local staffing and diagnostic protocols may differ.
inferred_scenario_use: Use acuity as a routing/priority attribute and configure role/equipment bundles as explicit scenario parameters. Do not use percentages or slots as RWJ facts.

source_setting: One US metropolitan ED; 27 treatment rooms; shared X-ray, clinical laboratory and pharmacy
quantity: Modeled task precedence and repeated role use

value.revisit: ESI 1–4 receive second nurse and physician/PA visit in this model

unit: ordered workflow states and result-ready gate
source_evidence_basis: The study’s process description states patients are first seen by a nurse, then a doctor orders tests, and after tests/results are ready a physician performs a final diagnostic visit. It says nurses and clinicians are used mostly twice depending on criticality; Table 2 assigns first and second visits.
limitations: This is the model’s chosen workflow for one ED. The paper assumes continuously available staff and fully operational diagnostic equipment; it does not validate a universal sequence for all presentations.
inferred_scenario_use: Represent separate clinician encounters and a result-ready condition before final interpretation/disposition; permit clinically specified alternate branches.

locator: Methods, IDEF-SIM conceptual model; Table 2 and accompanying note
source_setting: Canadian ED expansion plan; process/resource estimates from ED manager and nurses
quantity: Modeled AND/OR dependencies and tasks requiring all listed staff

value.logic: AND (&) means required parallel condition; OR (x) means alternative branch
all_staff_tasks: huddle: triage nurse + registration + ED nurse + physician + admin
value.other_joint_task: EHS call/triage assigns both triage nurse and ED nurse

unit: resource roles and logical gates; times not reused
source_evidence_basis: The authors define explicit AND/OR flow symbols and state that marked tasks require all staff indicated. Their table assigns both an ED nurse and physician to a medical procedure, and a five-role team to huddles. Their process only advances at conditions such as tests ready and required nurse/doctor evaluation.
limitations: These are manager/nurse Delphi estimates and a simulation design for a Canadian expansion, not direct timing observations or a universal staffing rule. Task staffing may be site-specific.
inferred_scenario_use: Implement task bundles as atomic acquire-all resource constraints and explicit AND gates for completion; retain alternate-path logic where stated.

locator: Table 2: Triage, register, nurse/physician assessment; Methods/data

value.test-result charting: ED nurse + admin role in modeled table

unit: assigned role per task; precedence states
source_evidence_basis: The study distinguishes triage, registration, nurse assessment, and physician assessment as separate tasks with distinct role assignments rather than one generic staff pool. The process map separately shows queues/delays and role requirements, allowing the simulation to seize the relevant resource for each activity.
limitations: Task durations are expert Delphi estimates, and listed roles represent this specific process design. The source does not establish RWJ job boundaries.
inferred_scenario_use: Keep roles separate in scenario resources; require the designated role for each task rather than interchangeable generic staff.

source_period: Study publication 2021; exact observation dates not present in inspected sections
source_n: 178 observed triage/initial-assessment cases with completed surveys; eligible adult patients except ESI 1 and specified exclusions
source_title: Interruption of initial patient assessment in the emergency department and its effect on patient perception of care quality
locator: Abstract; Methods and Results, TIAT observations
source_setting: Academic Level I trauma center, Midwestern United States; 55 ED beds, adult ED
quantity: Observed triage interruption occurrence and consequence association

value.direction: higher interruption frequency associated with increased errors; interruptions lengthened triage duration

unit: percent of observed cases; qualitative associations
source_evidence_basis: Prospective time-motion observations found that 62.9% of 178 observations were interrupted one to five times. More interruptions were associated with increased errors, and interruptions increased triage duration; duration was negatively associated with satisfaction. The study separately recorded source, cause, interrupted task, provider reaction, errors, triage duration, and interruption duration.
limitations: Single academic site, excludes highest-acuity ESI 1 and several vulnerable/non-English groups; association does not quantify a general causal effect or transferable interruption rate.
inferred_scenario_use: Make assessment interruption a possible event that pauses/switches task, tracks unfinished items, and can trigger recheck/rework; avoid assigning this cohort’s frequency to the scenario.

source_title: Guidance for emergency departments: initial assessment
quantity: Handover ownership and conditional turnaround target

value.responsibility: hospital clinical responsibility begins on ambulance arrival

unit: minutes from arrival; prescribed target and ownership rule
source_evidence_basis: NHS England distinguishes pre-alerted patients needing a clinical team, who should be received immediately, from non-pre-alerted arrivals, whose handover should be completed within 15 minutes through locally agreed processes. It states hospital clinical responsibility starts at department arrival.
limitations: Prescriptive England guidance, not observed compliance, individual handover-time distribution, or US/RWJ policy.
inferred_scenario_use: Model arrival, clinical ownership, and handover completion as separate timestamped events; treat 15 minutes as an external policy target only, and ensure administrative steps do not delay clinical ownership.

source_title: Evaluating alternative resource allocation in an emergency department using discrete event simulation
source_setting: One US metropolitan ED; model uses ESI 1–5

value.priority_attribute: ED-specific ESI acuity/resource category, levels 1 (most urgent) through 5 (least urgent)
value.routing: ESI3 physician; ESI4-5 PA in this model

unit: ordinal acuity categories and role routing
source_evidence_basis: In the studied ED, nurses assigned ESI levels 1–5, with level 1 most urgent and level 5 least urgent. The model routes level 3 patients to physicians and levels 4–5 to physician assistants and assigns different expected resources by level.
limitations: This is one ED’s implementation, not a universal priority queue discipline, and the paper does not establish exact preemption behavior.
inferred_scenario_use: Use acuity as an explicit selection attribute for the synthetic encounter queue; make tie-breaking and interruption/preemption separate configurable rules rather than implying the source prescribes them.

source_period: Arrival data drawn from fall and winter; exact calendar dates not stated; 2016 publication
source_n: One ED model; 27 treatment rooms reported
source_title: Evaluating alternative resource allocation in an emergency department using discrete event simulation
locator: Section 3.1, process description and modeled ED assets
source_setting: One US metropolitan ED, open 24 hours; shares diagnostics and pharmacy with hospital
quantity: Reported treatment-room pool and shared diagnostic assets
source_evidence_basis: The paper describes a 27-room ED, including two rooms equipped for CPR, two for inmates, and one for psychological patients, with X-ray, laboratory, and pharmacy shared with the hospital. These are setting characteristics stated in the source, distinct from its staffing allocation experiments.
limitations: A single-site paper’s inventory description; not current RWJ inventory, staffing, live availability, or proof all rooms are suitable for a specific synthetic case.
inferred_scenario_use: Use room types and shared diagnostics as candidate resource categories in an external scenario configuration. Never transfer the counts to RWJ or interpret them as available capacity.
